name: pet-shelter
description: Open-source adoption and rescue platform for animal shelters, with ISO 11784/11785 microchip identity tracking

scripts.//deploy:storage-rules: `firebase deploy --only storage` CANNOT deploy this project's storage.rules — it demands a Firebase DEFAULT bucket and we deliberately use a named, Terraform-managed one. See scripts/release-storage-rules.mjs.
scripts.//seed:pet: Publish one pet: validates the document, strips EXIF from the photo, uploads it, and DERIVES coverPhoto from the upload. See scripts/seed-pet.mjs. Usage: npm run seed:pet -- seed/luna.json
scripts.//test: node --test globs do not work on Node 20, so every test file is named explicitly. Revisit when this machine moves to Node 22.
scripts.test: node --test --import tsx src/lib/__tests__/microchip.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/placements.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/arrival.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/intake.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/readmission.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/areas.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/intake-suggestion.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/pricing.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/dictation.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/medical.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/suggest-budget.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/intake-suggest-client.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/i18n-es.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/model-ladder.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/intake-prompt.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/spanish-register.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/measurements.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/review-gate.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/medical-gate.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/card-extraction.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/card-prompt.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/card-extract-budget.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/medical-wiring.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/medical-candidates.test.ts
scripts.//grant:admin: Grant/revoke the admin custom auth claim, the thing firestore.rules and storage.rules gate every write on. Needs GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set. Usage: npm run grant:admin -- someone@example.com  |  -- --list
scripts.//ai:probe: Verify the Gemini setup: is there a key, does it work, and do the model IDs in src/lib/ai/model-ids.ts actually exist for that key? Those IDs came from a SIBLING project and have never been checked here. Never prints the key. Usage: npm run ai:probe  |  -- --call
scripts.//eval:intake: Score photo-assisted intake against a known animal in _e2e/. Calls the REAL suggestFromPhoto, so it measures production rather than a copy of it. Bare invocation is a DRY RUN that prints what it would spend; --run actually calls the model at 1 free-tier request per model. --conditions=react-server is what lets the `server-only` import resolve to a no-op outside Next; without it the import throws. Usage: npm run eval:intake  |  -- --run  |  -- --run --models a,b
scripts.//probe:suggest: Answer ONE question: when a four-photo intake 'hangs', is the socket dead or is the call slow and we abort too early? Every production failure sits on OUR 25s abort, so nobody has seen what the provider does at 90s. Measures latency and failure shape only — it does NOT score answers (that is eval:intake) and does NOT go through Firebase Hosting. Bare invocation is a DRY RUN. Usage: npm run probe:suggest  |  -- --run  |  -- --run --photos 1 --n 8  |  -- --run --model gemini-3.1-flash-lite --n 20
scripts.//cards:synthesize: Draw synthetic Bolivian-style vaccination cards and their answer key into _e2e/cards/ (gitignored). SYNTHETIC cards are easier than real ones: scores on them are an UPPER BOUND. Usage: npm run cards:synthesize
scripts.//eval:cards: Score vaccination-card extraction against the synthetic cards. Calls the REAL extractFromCard and reviewCardExtraction, so it measures what a reviewer would be shown. Bare invocation is a DRY RUN; --run spends one request per card x model x rep. Refuses to run if the answer key has leaked into the prompt. Usage: npm run eval:cards  |  -- --run --models gemini-3.1-flash-lite
scripts.//probe:card-rules: Evaluate the DEPLOYED Firestore and Storage rules against the card-extraction writes and reads, through the Firebase Rules test API. Releases nothing and writes nothing. Usage: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=wawitas npm run probe:card-rules
